in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex, who's 16 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's great to know about Alex.

Since Alex is 16, I need to ask a few more questions to determine eligibility.

Is Alex currently in full-time education or approved training? (This is important because for children aged 16-19, Child Benefit can continue if they remain in qualifying education or training.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he actually just left school recently, but he's signed up with the local careers service to figure out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. This is helpful information.

When you say Alex has "just left school recently" and is now signed up with the local careers service - could you tell me a bit more about his current situation?

Specifically:
- Has Alex started any new education course, training programme, or employment since leaving school?
- Or is he currently not in education, training, or work while he decides his next steps?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's not in any education, training, or work at the moment. He's just taking some time to figure out what he wants to do next while working with the careers service.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Based on what you've told me, I have some good news!

Since Alex is 16 years old and has recently left education but is now registered with the local careers service (a government-sponsored careers service), you may be able to continue receiving Child Benefit for him.

According to the rules, you can apply for Child Benefit to continue for **20 weeks** if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with either:
- A government-sponsored careers service
- The armed services

I just have a couple more questions to confirm your eligibility:

1. Do you live in the UK?
2. Does Alex live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK and Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for confirming that. I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why:

**For Alex (age 16):**
- ✅ You live in the UK
- ✅ Alex lives with you, so you're responsible for him
- ✅ Although Alex has left school, he is registered with the local careers service (a government-sponsored careers service)

Because Alex is 16-17 and registered with a government-sponsored careers service, you can apply to continue receiving Child Benefit for **up to 20 weeks** while he decides on his next steps.

**Important things to note:**
- This 20-week extension is designed to give Alex time to figure out his next move
- If Alex starts approved education or training within this period, you may continue to be eligible beyond the 20 weeks
- If Alex starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week, starts an apprenticeship in England, or begins receiving certain benefits like Universal Credit, your Child Benefit would stop

I hope this helps! If you have any further questions or Alex's circumstances change, you can always contact the Child Benefit Office for more guidance.
